rows.selection_reason: No experiments are completed yet, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple unimodal baseline has predictive signal and which design axis to anchor future comparisons. config_001 tests RNA-only, single-profile PCA as the minimal RNA baseline, isolating modality and representation without multiprofile aggregation or fusion. It is the best next experiment because it is low-cost, avoids confounding complexity, and provides a reference for later evaluating RNA encoders, multiprofile aggregation, and multimodal fusion.

Only a single RNA-only PCA single-profile baseline is available, so it is still unknown whether image features carry independent predictive signal. config_010 tests image-only single-profile ResNet50 without aggregation or fusion, providing a clean unimodal image baseline comparable in profile complexity to config_001. This is the best next use of budget because it reduces uncertainty about the modality axis before spending experiments on multimodal fusion, multiprofile aggregation, or heavier encoders.

The only strong result so far is RNA-only with PCA n2000 in single-profile mode, while image-only ResNet50 is weak. The key uncertainty is whether adding multiple profiles helps the promising RNA modality, and whether a simple aggregation method is enough. config_002 keeps the same RNA encoder and tests multiprofile with avgpool, isolating the profile/aggregation effect before trying more complex transformer aggregation or multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA with avgpool (config_002) improves substantially over singleprofile RNA (config_001), while image-only ResNet is weak. The main uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can further improve the promising multiprofile RNA setting. Testing config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, isolating that effect and efficiently guiding later multimodal design choices.

RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool is the current best configuration (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), clearly above singleprofile PCA and transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet is very weak. The key uncertainty is whether a stronger RNA representation can improve on PCA under the best profile/aggregation setting. config_008 tests the scGPT RNA encoder while keeping multiprofile avgpool fixed, isolating the effect of representation. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest unimodal direction with a single-factor change, has higher expected accuracy than image-only tests, and avoids premature multimodal/fusion testing while image evidence remains weak.

The strongest evidence is that RNA-only multiprofile with PCA and avgpool is the best current setup (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), while transformer aggregation and scGPT are weaker, and image-only ResNet is very weak (0.208 accuracy). The key uncertainty is whether adding image information to the proven RNA setup can improve validation accuracy. config_018 keeps the best known RNA representation, profile, and aggregation fixed while adding ResNet image features with simple concat fusion, directly testing whether multimodal fusion helps under the current strongest baseline. This is the best next use of budget because it exploits the strongest evidence while clarifying whether image modality is worth further exploration before trying more complex ViT or weighted-fusion variants.

The current best result is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet, avgpool, concat) with validation accuracy 0.6186 and F1 0.6103, but it only modestly improves over the RNA-only multiprofile PCA avgpool baseline (0.5907), and image-only ResNet is weak. This leaves uncertainty about whether concat fusion is the best way to combine modalities or whether weighted fusion can better balance the stronger RNA signal with the weaker image signal. config_019 tests only the fusion choice while keeping the rest of the best-performing setup fixed, making it a clean exploitation experiment that can either improve the current best or clarify whether concat is already sufficient.

The strongest completed result is config_019, a multimodal multiprofile model with PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, and weighted fusion, reaching 0.639 accuracy and 0.620 F1, above the best RNA-only avgpool model and the concat-fusion multimodal model. RNA-only evidence also suggests avgpool is preferable to transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion appears slightly better than concat, so those settings should be kept. The main remaining uncertainty in this promising direction is the image encoder: ResNet50 was weak as an image-only model, yet it still helped in multimodal fusion. Testing config_025 changes only the image encoder to ViT-L while preserving the best-known RNA encoder, profile setting, aggregation, and fusion. This isolates the effect of image representation, exploits the current best configuration, and has high potential immediate value by clarifying whether a stronger image encoder can improve the leading multimodal setup.

The strongest evidence is config_019, a multimodal multiprofile PCA + ResNet50 + avgpool + weighted model with 0.639 accuracy and 0.620 F1, slightly better than concat and ViT variants. RNA-only PCA results suggest avgpool is stronger than transformer, but it remains unclear whether transformer aggregation could improve the best multimodal pipeline. config_021 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the best fusion, image encoder, profile setting, and RNA encoder, cleanly isolating the aggregation effect in the most promising setting.

The strongest evidence is that multimodal multiprofile models with PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, and weighted fusion perform best (config_019: 0.6390 acc / 0.6197 F1), with weighted fusion and avgpool clearly favored over concat and transformer in comparable settings. The main remaining uncertainty is whether a learned RNA encoder can improve on PCA in this best-performing multimodal setup; scvi is untested. config_031 changes only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while holding profile, image encoder, aggregation, and fusion fixed, making it a clean one-factor test. It is the best next use of budget because it exploits the current best configuration while efficiently reducing uncertainty about RNA representation quality.
